etymology.root: French négociant, a trader, from Latin negotiari, to do business

text.what: A merchant who buys grapes, juice or finished wine, raises it in their own cellar and sells it under their own name. Half of Burgundy's output moves this way.
text.how: A négociant-éleveur raises what it buys. A domaine bottles only its own fruit. Many houses do both and the label says which is which, if you read the small print.

kin.as: A house that grew into a large grower as well.
Where the trade is structured around this.
